newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Stals warns rates may have to rise.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Stals warns rates may have to rise.

text.p: South African Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals said on Friday that an even more stringent monetary policy might be needed to curb liquidity and excessive credit growth.
The central bank remained committed to reducing the monetary stimulation of inflation during 1997, Stals told a conference.

"Recent trends in the money supply and bank credit extension beg the question, however, whether monetary policy at this juncture is restrictive enough and whether even more stringent measures may not be required to reduce overall liquidity further, which could, of course, lead to even higher interest rates and hopefully also a decline in the demand for credit," he said.
The authorities remained "greatly concerned" about the latest trends in the rate of increase in money supply, bank credit extension and inflation, Stals said.
There was a real danger that price increases in the wake of last year's fall in the rand could become embedded in a permanently higher rate of inflation, he said.
The Reserve Bank is due to release March money supply and credit data at 1500 GMT on Friday.

Economists polled by Reuters predicted a 16.50 percent increase in private sector credit extension growth compared with a preliminary 17.34 percent rise in February. Money supply growth is expected to show a 15.04 pecent year-on-year rise from February's preliminary 15.82 percent.
March consumer price inflation stood at an annual rate of 9.6 percent in March, marginally down on February's 9.8 percent. But the rate has risen sharply from the 24-year low of April lastt year.
South Africa's official Bank rate currently stands at 17.0 percent, following a one point hike last November, while commercial banks' prime lending rate is 20.25 percent.
